abstract: 1. A CK(BB) fraction was observed in sera of a patient with prostatic carcinoma. The fraction accounted for 59% of the total enzyme activity. A metastatic tumor of a prostatic carcinoma was observed to contain solely the CK(BB) isozyme. An embryonal testicular carcinoma was observed to have a higher percentage of the CK(BB) fraction when compared to the adjacent tumor free testicular tissue in a third patient. These studies suggested that in certain carcinomas there are tissue isozyme modifications at the molecular level. The isozymic modification was suggested as a reversion towards an embroyonic pattern as the adult molecular form tended to disappear while the fetal form increased. This too suggests that the isozymes of CK may be a useful model in elucidating the mechanism through which this transition occurs. 2. The high percentage of CK(BB) in the sera of the patient with metastasis was discussed. The origin could not be determined, but either a primary tumor or a metastatic tumor by their enzyme modifications could account for this increased fraction in sera.
abstract_ja: 1. 前立腺がん患者の血清にCK（BB）分画が認められた。この分画は全酵素活性の59%を占めた。転移性前立腺がんの腫瘍組織はCK（BB）アイソザイムのみを含んでいた。別の患者では、胎児性精巣がんの腫瘍部が隣接する腫瘍のない精巣組織よりもCK（BB）分画の割合が高かった。これらの研究は、ある種の癌では組織アイソザイムが分子レベルで修飾されることを示唆する。成人型の分子形は減少し、胎児型が増加することから、この修飾は胎児型パターンへの復帰と解釈された。2. 転移を有する患者の血清中CK（BB）分画の高値について考察した。その起源は特定できなかったが、原発腫瘍または転移腫瘍のいずれかの酵素修飾が、血清中の分画増加を説明しうる。
